title: Random spin-3/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains revisited
authors: Yen-Tung Lin, Pochung Chen, Yu-Cheng Lin
abstract: We revisit the spin-reduction transition in the random spin-$3/2$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain using the tensor-network strong-disorder renormalization group (tSDRG). The predicted transition separates two random-singlet (RS) phases: one formed by effective spin-$1/2$ moments at weaker disorder and the other by full spin-$3/2$ moments at stronger disorder. Within the Damle--Huse classification, this transition corresponds to an emergent permutation-symmetric $\mathcal{P}_4$ multicritical point on a $\mathcal{P}_2$ critical line associated with the RS phases. We first derive the critical exponents governing the disorder-averaged bulk and end-to-end correlation functions in the $\mathcal{P}_n$ universality classes within the Damle--Huse framework. Using these theoretical predictions, together with a diagnostic constructed from the mean and variance of the energy-gap distribution, we identify the $\mathcal{P}_4$ transition point and the reentrant behavior of the RS phase.
summary: This work theoretically investigates the spin-reduction transition in random spin-3/2 Heisenberg chains using the tSDRG method. It maps this transition onto a specific $\mathcal{P}_4$ multicritical point within the Damle--Huse universality class. The study successfully predicts and confirms the critical exponents governing the system's correlation functions at this disorder-driven quantum critical point.
main_problem: The paper revisits the spin-reduction transition in the random spin-3/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain, characterizing the critical point using advanced renormalization group techniques.
main_result: The transition is identified as corresponding to a $\mathcal{P}_4$ multicritical point within the Damle--Huse classification, yielding specific theoretical critical exponents ($\eta=1, \eta_1=1/2$).
method: The study employs the Tensor-Network Strong-Disorder Renormalization Group (tSDRG) method combined with theoretical derivations from the Damle--Huse RG framework.
model_or_system: The system is a random spin-3/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain, modeled by random couplings $J_i$ and analyzed through its low-energy effective degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Bulk and end-to-end correlation functions ($C_b(r) \sim r^{-\eta}$, $C_1(L) \sim L^{-\eta_1}$), and the energy gap distribution.
important_parameters: Bond randomness strength ($R$), which controls the system's location relative to the critical point ($R_c \approx 0.9$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Damle--Huse classification of infinite-randomness fixed points and the applicability of the tSDRG method to capture asymptotic critical scaling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the domain-wall RG processes, show numerical agreement between calculated and theoretical critical exponents for $P_n$ classes, and map out phase diagrams in the randomness parameter space.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the Damle--Huse RG theory, derives flow equations for domain couplings, and then applies the tSDRG method to calculate critical exponents and locate the $P_4$ multicritical point by analyzing correlation function scaling and gap distributions.
why_interesting: The application of advanced RG techniques (tSDRG) to characterize quantum phase transitions in highly disordered magnetic systems provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding quantum criticality in materials science.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Two decimation processes in the Damle–Huse domain-wall RG. In the same-type (σ′ = σ′′) process, the domain-wall spins at sites i and j, which bound the domain with the strongest coupling, form a singlet, and that domain is eliminated. In the different-type (σ′ ̸= σ′′) process, the two domain walls at i and j merge into a single domain wall carrying the effective spin Sσ′,σ′′ given by Eq. (3). Throughout the RG, the size s(i) of spin cluster associated with each domain wall is also tracked.

Figure 2. Disorder-averaged correlations at the Pn fixed point, with n = 3, 4 and 5, obtained by numerical domain-wall RG. (a) Disorder-averaged bulk correlations for spins separated by the largest distance L/2 in chains with periodic boundary conditions; (b) disorder-averaged end-to-end correlations in open chains. For each parameter n and system size L, 300,000 samples (disorder realizations) were used to obtain the averaged correlations.
Figure 4. Distributions of energy gaps at R = 0.1. (a) Unscaled log-histograms for system sizes L = 256, 512, and 1024; (b) A scaling plot of the gap-histograms, assuming −ln(∆E) ∼Lψ with ψ = 1/2.

Figure 5. The ratio (B) of the variance of the energy gap to the mean energy gap, plotted as a function of R for system sizes L = 128(inset), 256, 512, and 1024. The minimum around R = 0.9 indicates a transition point.

Figure 6. Distributions of energy gaps at Rc = 0.9. (a) Unscaled log-histograms for L = 256, 512, and 1024; (b) A scaling plot of the gap-histograms with ψ4 = 1/4, corresponding to the P4 universality class; (c) Rescaled histograms with ψ2 = 1/2 exhibit poor data collapse.
